When dealing with command execution in C++ programs, it is important to be aware of potential vulnerabilities such as command injection. Here are some best practices to mitigate the risk of command injection vulnerabilities:

1. Avoid using user input directly in commands: Do not concatenate user input directly into the command string. Instead, validate and sanitize user input before using it in a command.

2. Use parameterized commands: If you need to include dynamic values in a command, consider using parameterized commands or APIs provided by the operating system or libraries. This can help prevent command injection by automatically escaping special characters.

3. Limit the scope of commands: Only execute commands that are necessary for the functionality of your program. Avoid running arbitrary commands or commands with excessive privileges.

4. Validate input and output: Validate the input to your program to ensure it meets expected criteria. Also, validate the output of commands to prevent unexpected behavior.

5. Use secure coding practices: Follow secure coding practices such as input validation, output encoding, and proper error handling to reduce the risk of command injection vulnerabilities.

By following these best practices, you can help protect your C++ program from command injection vulnerabilities and improve its overall security.

VMware Workstation Pro (known as VMware Workstation until release of VMware Workstation 12 in 2015) is a hosted (Type 2) hypervisor that runs on x64 versions of Windows and Linux operating systems. It enables users to set up virtual machines (VMs) on a single physical machine and use them simultaneously along with the host machine. Each virtual machine can execute its own operating system, including versions of Microsoft Windows, Linux, BSD, and MS-DOS. VMware Workstation is developed and sold by VMware, which has been owned by Broadcom since November 2023. In May 2024, Workstation Pro became free of charge for personal use, with paid subscriptions available for commercial use, while the free restricted VMware Workstation Player (formerly known as VMware Player) was dropped.  In November 2024, VMware Workstation was made free for commercial use, with paid subscriptions and support no longer available.
VMware Workstation supports bridging existing host network adapters and sharing physical disk drives and USB devices with a virtual machine. It can simulate disk drives; an ISO image file can be mounted as a virtual optical disc drive, and virtual hard disk drives are implemented as .vmdk files.
VMware Workstation Pro can save the state of a virtual machine (a "snapshot") at any instant. These snapshots can later be restored, effectively returning the virtual machine to the saved state, as it was and free from any post-snapshot damage to the VM.
VMware Workstation includes the ability to group multiple virtual machines in an inventory folder. The machines in such a folder can then be powered on and powered off as a single object, useful for testing complex client-server environments.
